Q1: Benzoyl chloride presents significant known hazards across most categories, including carcinogenicity, mutagenicity and reproductive hazards (CMR), environmental, inhalation, oral, dermal, eye, and organ/systemic hazards, all rated Tier 1. It is rated Tier 3 for endocrine disruption hazards, indicating a demonstrated low to moderate concern in this area.
Q2: Benzoyl chloride is identified as a hazardous substance under the Clean Water Act, indicating known environmental concerns. It does not appear on any lists specifically designating it as a low-hazard chemical.
Q3: Benzoyl chloride is extensively characterized, with a very high number of scientific literature references and a well-defined molecular structure. While it has a moderate number of aggregated toxicity records, it has not undergone the most rigorous formal evaluations by EPA's IRIS or PPRTV programs.
